topic: What interference mitigation techniques are viable for overlapping service transmissions across geographically dispersed ground stations?
consensus_response: To mitigate interference between geographically dispersed ground stations, Analog Beamforming can be employed to dynamically adjust antenna patterns and reduce cochannel interference. Additionally, Rate Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) can split each user's data into two streams: one common stream shared among all users and another private stream for individual users. This approach reduces cochannel interference while improving capacity. Furthermore, Digital Predistortion (DPD) can be applied to mitigate nonlinearities in power amplifiers, reducing intermodulation distortion and adjacent channel leakage ratio (ACLR). By integrating these techniques, the detrimental effects of multipath interference and cochannel interference can be minimized, ensuring high integrity transmission in safety-critical aeronautical applications.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the importance of mitigating interference between geographically dispersed ground stations. Statistics from Scotland show that up to 24.3% of areas experience no reliable 2G signal from any operator. Research on Analog Beamforming, Rate Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA), and Digital Predistortion (DPD) suggests these techniques can effectively reduce cochannel interference.
